get_device_status: Get the operational status and health information of a network device. Returns device uptime, CPU usage, memory usage, and overall health status.
get_device_interfaces: List all network interfaces on a device. Note: For most queries, prefer query_device_info tool.
get_interface_details: Get interface details. Note: For most queries, prefer query_device_info tool.
get_device_vlans: Get VLAN configuration. Note: For most queries, prefer query_device_info tool.
execute_device_command: Execute a generic command or API call on a device. This is a flexible tool for operations not covered by specific tools. Use only when other tools don't provide the needed functionality.
search_documentation: Search device documentation, CLI references, and API guides to answer 'how-to' questions and provide command syntax help. Use this when users ask questions about device features, configuration procedures, or need to understand command syntax. IMPORTANT: You MUST cite sources for all information retrieved from documentation. Use the format [Source: filename, Page X] for every fact or command you provide. If no relevant documentation is found, explicitly state that the information is not available in the current documentation and suggest where the user might find it.
diagnose_port_issues: Perform comprehensive diagnostics to troubleshoot why a port is down or having issues, AND to view syslog events and recent activity for a port. USE THIS TOOL when users ask about: recent events, syslog, event log, port history, port issues, connectivity problems, or port diagnostics. This tool analyzes multiple data sources including: current port status, interface error counters, PoE status (if applicable), cable diagnostics test results, and historical syslog events. It automatically detects patterns like link flapping, PoE power cycling, error storms, and configuration-related issues. Use this tool when users ask about port down problems, connectivity issues, or need help diagnosing why a device connected to a port isn't working. Example queries: 'What are recent events on port 4?', 'Show syslog for port 5', 'Why is port 5 down?', 'Diagnose connectivity issue on port 3', 'What's wrong with the camera on port 7?', 'Port 2 keeps flapping', 'Show event log for port 1'
get_camera_detections: Query what a camera is currently detecting, or look up detection history. Use mode='live' to sample the stream right now . Use mode='history' to query the SQLite log for past detections . When the user mentions a specific camera by name or location, supply camera_id. camera1 (Entrance Camera) does object detection — available COCO labels: person, backpack, suitcase, handbag, car, truck, motorcycle, bicycle, bottle, laptop, cell-phone, knife, scissors, etc. camera2 (Loading Bay Camera) does gesture/pose detection — available labels: left-hand-raised, right-hand-raised. Use the appropriate labels based on which camera the user is asking about.
get_network_events: Query recent network events from the PoE switch syslog feed. Use this when users ask about network activity, switch events, PoE events, link state changes, authentication failures, or any switch log history. Examples: 'what happened on the network in the last 5 minutes?', 'any PoE events recently?', 'show link-down events', 'did anything happen on the switch today?'
calibrate_cable_baseline: Calibrate and store a cable length baseline for a switch port. Run this when a cable is healthy and connected to establish a reference length. Later, diagnose_port_issues will compare measured lengths against the baseline to identify where a cable break or disconnect occurred (near-end, midpoint, or far-end). Only works when cable test result is OK/Normal.
show_port_status: Show port link status, speed, duplex, and operational state for one port.
show_all_ports_status: Show link status, speed, duplex, and operational state for all ports.
show_poe_status: Show PoE power status and usage for one port.
show_all_poe_status: Show PoE status and power usage for all ports.
show_poe_config: Show PoE configuration (mode, priority, max power) for one port.
show_all_poe_config: Show PoE configuration (mode, priority, max power) for all ports.
show_poe_power_budget: Show PoE power budget (total/available/used power) for the switch.
show_cable_diagnostics: Run a cable diagnostics test (link status, test result, cable length) on one port.
show_all_cable_diagnostics: Run a cable diagnostics test on all ports.
show_vlan_config: Show detailed per-port VLAN configuration (PVID, Frame Type, Ingress Filter, Tx Tag).
show_vlan_membership: Show VLAN summary of member ports and untagged ports.
show_system_info: Show switch model, version, uptime, and system details.
show_ip_interface: Show IP address configuration for the management interface.
enable_port: Enable a disabled network port (interface link, no-shutdown).
disable_port: Disable a network port (interface link, shutdown) -- cuts all traffic.
configure_poe_mode: Enable or disable PoE power delivery on a port (data link is unaffected).
configure_port_speed: Set the speed of a network port.
configure_port_duplex: Set the duplex mode of a network port.
configure_access_vlan: Assign a VLAN to an access port.
configure_poe_power_limit: Set the maximum PoE power limit for a port (1-30W).
set_port_description: Set a description label for a port.
configure_trunk_allowed_vlans: Set a port to trunk mode and configure which VLANs are allowed on it.
create_vlan: Create a new VLAN on the switch.
